stem: Which of the following does not belong to the solar system?
expl: The solar system was formed around 4.6 billion years ago. The solar system consists of the sun (star), cosmic dust or masses attached to each other by gravitational force, planets, dwarf planets, natural planetoids, asteroids, comets, meteoroids and cosmic dust while nebulae are not a part of the Solar System.

stem: Who first propounded that the Sun is the center of our Solar system and the earth revolves around it?
expl: Nicolaus Copernicus was an astronomer and mathematician from Poland. Copernicus propounded the Heliocentric Theory of the solar system in his essay 'Commentariolus' (Little Commentary). Notably, Indian astronomer Varahamihira propounded the same theory around a thousand years before Copernicus in the sixth century. He mentioned that the moon revolves around the earth and the earth revolves around the sun.

stem: Which one of the following statements is correct with reference to our solar system?

options.label: a
options.text: The Earth is the densest of all the planets in our solar system

options.label: b
options.text: The predominant element in the composition of Earth is silicon

options.label: c
options.text: The Sun contains 75 percent of the mass of the solar system

options.label: d
options.text: The diameter of the Sun is 190 times that of the Earth

expl: The average density of Earth is highest among all the other eight planets of our Solar System. It is 5.5 gm/cm3 . The density of other planets is as follows (Unit–gm/ cm3) Mercury (5.4), Venus (5.2), Mars (3.9), Jupiter (1.3), Saturn (0.7) Uranus (1.3), Neptune (1.6). Thus statement (a) is correct. The largest constituent element of Earth is Iron (32.07%). Oxygen (30.12%) is the second and Silicon (15.12%) is the third largest element in the composition of Earth. The sun comprises 99.8% mass of the solar system. The diameter of the sun is about 109.2 times the Earth's diameter.

stem: The number of the planet in the solar system is –
expl: According to old recognition, there are a total of 9 planets which are in increasing order of distance from the sun, as follows : (i) Mercury (57.9 million km) (ii) Venus (108.2 million km) (iii) Earth (149.6 million km) (iv) Mars (228 million km) (v) Jupiter (778.5 million km) (vi) Saturn (1432 million km) (vii) Uranus (2867 million km) (viii) Neptune (4515 million km) (ix) Pluto (5906.4 million km) Note : In the 26th General Assembly meeting of the International Astronomical Union held at Prague in 2006 an official definition of a planet was given and a resolution was passed by which Pluto has been removed from the group of 9 planets and now it is a dwarf planet. Hence, the total number of planets is 8 now.

stem: 'The term 'Goldilocks Zone' is often seen in the news in the context of

options.label: a
options.text: The limits of the habitable zone above the surface of the Earth

options.label: b
options.text: Regions inside the Earth where shale gas is available

options.label: c
options.text: Search for the Earth-like planets in outer space

options.label: d
options.text: Search for meteorites containing precious metals

expl: In astronomy, the circumstellar habituable zone is also called 'Goldilocks Zone'. It refers to the habitable zone around a star where the temperature is just right- not too hot and not too cold for liquid water to exist on a planet. Earth is the only planet inhabiting life in the entire solar system. It is the only planet situated in the Goldilocks zone of the solar system.

stem:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the solar system?
I. Mercury is the hottest planet in the solar system
II. Ganymede, satellite of Saturn, is the largest satellite in the solar system
III. Neptune is surrounded by methane gas rings of sub-zero temperature
IV. Phobos and Deimos are two satellites of Mars

options.label: a
options.text: Only I and II are correct

options.label: b
options.text: Only II and III are correct

options.label: c
options.text: Only III and IV are correct

options.label: d
options.text: I, II, III and IV all are correct

expl: Venus is the hottest planet in the solar system, not Mercury. This is, because its dense atmosphere acts as a greenhouse and heats the surface to about 464ºC. Ganymede is the largest satellite in the solar system, but it is a satellite of Jupiter, not Saturn. Neptune is surrounded by methane gas rings of sub-zero temperature. Mars has two small moons : Phobos and Deimos.
